title: When the Songbook Breaks
premise: Silas Eastwick abandoned his singing career after a scandal destroyed his mentor's festival and took his voice with it — but he never stopped answering the anonymous letters that arrived every year on the anniversary, letters signed only 'the songbook.' When the letter-writer, Wren Calloway, moves in next door and begins organizing the festival's revival, Silas is hired to plan it, forcing him back into the world he fled. As their intimacy deepens, Silas discovers Wren was the whistleblower whose testimony saved him but condemned the man they both loved. At the festival's closing night, Silas finally speaks the rehearsed sentence — a confession of love and forgiveness — choosing memory over the safe silence he built his life on.
about_author: Coral Eriksen is a former choral librarian who spent a decade cataloguing other people's songs before writing her own stories. She lives in a coastal town where she still attends every wedding she's invited to, just to watch the vows.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the anniversary of the scandal, the tenth letter arrives — and this time it includes a forwarding address: the cottage next door. Silas watches Wren Calloway unpack boxes of festival archives through his window, recognizing handwriting he's memorized for a decade. Emotional beat: dread tangled with longing, as seven years of careful distance collapse in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: Everything Must Be Planned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren hires Silas to plan the festival's revival, pretending not to know him; Silas accepts, unable to refuse proximity. Planning meetings become charged with unspoken history — shared glances over seating charts, arguments about the program that are really about the past. Emotional beat: rising tension as both perform normalcy while the truth presses closer.

chapters.title: What the Whistle Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm traps them in the festival hall, and Wren confesses she wrote the letters out of guilt — her testimony ended the mentor who groomed them both, and saved Silas without his consent. Silas walks out into the rain. Emotional beat: the climax of revelation, where survival's price is finally named and love feels like betrayal.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The festival opens to a full house, and Wren prepares to leave town, believing she's lost him. Instead Silas takes the stage, breaks his decade of silence, and speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud — naming what happened, what she did, and what he chooses now. Emotional beat: cathartic resolution; power surrendered, memory reclaimed, two survivors stepping into an unwritten song together.
